claim_verdicts.evidence: v1.34 page: "All Kubernetes objects are stored in etcd." refs mirror (same section): "The snapshot file contains all the Kubernetes state and critical information." The rewind to the snapshot moment is also shown by the captured run (outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/etcd-snapshot.txt): `after`, created after the snapshot, is NotFound after the restore.

etcd v3.6 FAQ (WebFetch summary, quoted): "Cluster data must be replicated across all peers, so there will be bandwidth cost as well." and "Raft enforces cluster consistency." A committed write (including a delete) is therefore present on every member, so adding members does not protect against a wrong change.

v1.34 page: etcdctl "is the primary command-line client for interacting with etcd over a network"; etcdutl "is an administration utility designed to operate directly on etcd data files". refs mirror L65-67 adds: "...restoring snapshots, and validating data consistency". etcd v3.6 recovery guide: from v3.6 use "etcdutl to restore data from a snapshot".

v1.34 page, 'Snapshot using etcdctl options': `ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=<trusted-ca-file> --cert=<cert-file> --key=<key-file> snapshot save <backup-file-location>`. etcd v3.6 recovery: a snapshot may be "taken from a live member with the etcdctl snapshot save command". Run output at stage-3: "Snapshot saved at /var/lib/etcd/snapshot.db".

certificates.md: etcd-ca `etcd/ca.crt` is etcd's `--trusted-ca-file,--peer-trusted-ca-file`. ports-and-protocols.md: TCP 2379-2380 for etcd; setup-ha-etcd-with-kubeadm.md: peer URLs on :2380. Round 2: the lesson now says etcd "trusts" client certificates signed by the etcd CA, which is what --trusted-ca-file means. lifecycle.sh L31-34 (working tree): etcd_tls (--cacert/--cert/--key under /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd) is passed only to etcdctl, not etcdutl.

create-cluster-kubeadm.md L580: "etcd data directory configured by kubeadm is at `/var/lib/etcd` on the control-plane node." kubeadm-config.v1beta4: dataDir "Defaults to \"/var/lib/etcd\"". implementation-details.md L397: "make a `hostPath` mount out from the `dataDir` to the host's filesystem". kind-lifecycle-config.yaml @ stage-3 comment: "its data in /var/lib/etcd".

v1.34 page: "When restoring the cluster using etcdutl, use the --data-dir option to specify to which folder the cluster should be restored"; refs L432: "a directory that will be created during the restore process". etcd v3.6 recovery: "A cluster restore with etcdutl snapshot restore creates new etcd data directories", then "start etcd with the new data directories".

refs configure-upgrade-etcd.md L401-413: "stop all API server instances; restore state in all etcd instances; restart all API server instances" and "The Kubernetes project also recommends restarting Kubernetes components (`kube-scheduler`, `kube-controller-manager`, `kubelet`) to ensure that they don't rely on some stale data." Round 3 appositive "which runs the built-in control loops": controller.md L147-148 "built-in controllers that run inside the kube-controller-manager"; reference/_index.md L56 "Daemon that embeds the core control loops".

static-pod.md 'Dynamic addition and removal of static pods': "The running kubelet periodically scans the configured directory (`/etc/kubernetes/manifests` in our example) for changes and adds/removes Pods as files appear/disappear in this directory." The example moves the manifest out to /tmp and back.

kind design/initial (WebFetch): "Each \"node\" runs as a docker container." and "...before running kubeadm to initialize the node." Script facts as in round 1: etcd-snapshot.sh creates the cluster with --new, ConfigMap before, snapshot save, docker cp to backups/etcd/donhang-lifecycle.db, ConfigMap after, restore --data-dir /var/lib/etcd/restored, member -> member.before-restore. Captured output: VERSION v1.34.11.

outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/etcd-snapshot.txt L27-30: "$ kubectl get configmaps before after / NAME DATA AGE / before 1 ... / Error from server (NotFound): configmaps \"after\" not found". The lesson's output block matches this file line for line.

configure-upgrade-etcd: "All Kubernetes objects are stored in etcd." persistent-volumes.md: a PV is an API object that "captures the details of the implementation of the storage, be that NFS, iSCSI, or a cloud-provider-specific storage system". So etcd holds the object that describes the storage, while the data stays in that external storage.

secret.md: "Kubernetes Secrets are, by default, stored unencrypted in the API server's underlying data store (etcd). Anyone with API access can retrieve or modify a Secret, and so can anyone with access to etcd." v1.34 configure-upgrade-etcd: "In order to keep the sensitive Kubernetes data safe, encrypt the snapshot files."

configure-upgrade-etcd L285-287: "Periodically backing up the etcd cluster data is important to recover Kubernetes clusters under disaster scenarios, such as losing all control plane nodes." A copy kept only on a lost node cannot serve that purpose. The script does this at L22-26 (docker cp off the node).

Argo CD core concepts (WebFetch): Sync is "The process of making an application move to its target state. E.g. by applying changes to a Kubernetes cluster." Target state is "The desired state of an application, as represented by files in a Git repository." A sync applies one application's Git state and does not rewind other objects, while a restore does (claim 1). The comparison is conditioned on the objects being in the repository; round 1's "touches only those objects" is gone.

refs configure-upgrade-etcd.md L409-411: "The Kubernetes project also recommends restarting Kubernetes components (`kube-scheduler`, `kube-controller-manager`, `kubelet`) to ensure that they don't rely on some stale data." Round 3 §8 now names exactly these three components; round 2's "them" (controllers in general, read as operators) is gone. controller.md L147-148: built-in controllers "run inside the kube-controller-manager".
